newsitem.title: SWEDEN: ASSA ABLOY PURCHASE SECURES WARM WELCOME.
newsitem.headline: ASSA ABLOY PURCHASE SECURES WARM WELCOME.

text.p: Assa Abloy, the world's largest lock maker, secured swift market approval on Wednesday for its 1.1 billion franc ($189.5 million) purchase of French lock manufacturing group Vachette .

Assa Abloy shares soared 21 crowns to 172 crowns -- or 14 percent -- on news of the acquisition, which will be partly funded by a 640 million crown ($83 million) rights issue to existing shareholders.
"It is a good acquisition, and not too high a price for a good company," said analyst Jan Dworsky of C.I. Nordic Securities.
"This next major acquisition by Assa Abloy came a bit earlier than the market expected but it is in line with the company's strategy to expand within its core businesses."

Assa Abloy, whose 1997 sales are seen at over 5.6 billion crowns after rising 43 percent to 5.0 billion in 1996, said buying the Vachette group would enable the company to lift its operating margins by two to three percent within a few years.
"There is really good potential even if it takes a little time," Assa Abloy's managing director Carl-Henric Svanberg told a news conference.

The Vachette group consists of cylinder and lock makers JPM, Laperche, Bezault, and Litto, the leading lock and cylinder company in Belgium. Vachette's annual sales for 1997 are expected to exceed 1.1 billion French francs.
Poliet in the Saint Gobain group was the owner all of the Vachette businesses except for 50 percent of JPM, which is owned by the Italian lock company Fincisa.

But Svanberg said Poliet had not been interested in the business, although it was a good strategic buy for Assa Abloy, whose pre-tax profit soared 63 percent to 345 million crowns in 1996. "Through the acquisition Assa Abloy would strengthen
its position as the leading lock group in the world," Assa Abloy said in a statement.
It added the purchase was expected to have a positive impact on earnings per share from 1998 and ought to push group sales over the seven billion crown level.

Analyst Bo Engstrom from Carnegie said the acquisition was a good fit, giving Assa Abloy a large slice of the French and Belgium markets and access to French speaking countries in Africa -- new territory for the Swedish group.
"It a very good acquisition that fits very well into Assa Abloy's structure," Engstrom said.
Assa Abloy said the purchase would be partly financed through a rights issue and through an increase in Assa Abloy's existing multi-currency revolving bank credit facility.
The rights issue to existing shareholders would give one new share at 100 crowns each for 10 old shares, with the subscription period running from May 26 to June 13.
"Shareholders representing 43 percent of the share capital are positive to the rights issue," it said.
The company said the purchase would permit rationalisation and create synergies that will lead to profit improvements within a few years, with no negative impact in 1997.

"The business is well invested and is expected to generate a positive cash flow after acquisition costs already in 1997," Assa Abloy said. ($ = 5.804 French Francs) ($ = 7.695 Swedish Crowns) REUTER 161421 GMT apr 97
